chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man washing his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, from behind the cloth.'
ai.seo_question: Can a husband wash his deceased wife while she is wearing clothes?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from the chain of the Rawandis highlights the practical application of *awrah* (modesty) in funeral rites, specifically addressing the husband's role in washing his wife. The ruling to wash 'from behind the garment' underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving dignity and minimizing direct exposure during the ritual purification (*ghusl*) prior to burial.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man washing his wife. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, from behind the cloth’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man if he can give Ghusl (bath) to his dead wife from behind a cloth. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so from behind a cloth.’”
